classification.difficultyReason: Combine each pair of supplied membership descriptions using 'and' for intersection and inclusive 'or' for union, as explicitly requested.

content.prompt: Use the words ‘and’ and ‘or’ to describe the sets $P\cap Q$ and $P\cup Q$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: $P=\{\text{boys who play cricket}\}$, $Q=\{\text{boys who play tennis}\}$

answer.short:
$P\cap Q=\{\text{boys who play cricket and tennis}\}$.

$P\cup Q=\{\text{boys who play cricket or tennis}\}$.
answer.worked:
The intersection contains boys who belong to both sets: $P\cap Q=\{\text{boys who play cricket and tennis}\}$.

The union contains boys who belong to either set, including both: $P\cup Q=\{\text{boys who play cricket or tennis}\}$.
